ACTIVE MICRO-TOPIC: DIRECT/INDIRECT SPEECH, QUESTIONS AND IMPERATIVES.
STATUS: NEW FOCUSED SUB-PATTERN.

RULES
• Yes/no questions normally use if/whether.
• Wh-questions retain the question word but use statement order.
• Do/does/did normally disappears in reported questions.
• Commands use reporting verb + object + to + verb.
• Negative commands use object + not to + verb.
• Universal truths can retain present tense.

EXAMPLES
He said, "Are you ready?" → He asked me if I was ready.
She said, "Why are you late?" → She asked why I was late.
Father said to me, "Do not waste time." → Father advised me not to waste time.

10 FRESH QUESTIONS

Q1. He said to me, "Have you finished the assignment?"
A) He told me that I had finished the assignment.
B) He asked me if I had finished the assignment.
C) He asked me that I have finished the assignment.
D) He said me whether I finished the assignment.

Q2. She said to him, "Why are you late?"
A) She asked him why he was late.
B) She asked him why was he late.
C) She told him why he is late.
D) She asked that why he had late.

Q3. The officer said to the clerk, "Do not open the file."
A) The officer ordered the clerk do not open the file.
B) The officer told that the clerk did not open the file.
C) The officer instructed the clerk not to open the file.
D) The officer said the clerk not opened the file.

Q4. Rohan said, "Can I use your laptop?"
A) Rohan asked if he could use my laptop.
B) Rohan asked that can he use my laptop.
C) Rohan told me if I could use his laptop.
D) Rohan said whether he can use my laptop.

Q5. The teacher said to the students, "Why did you miss the class?"
A) The teacher asked the students why they had missed the class.
B) The teacher asked the students why had they missed the class.
C) The teacher told the students why they miss the class.
D) The teacher asked why did they miss the class.

Q6. Mother said to Anu, "Please close the window."
A) Mother ordered Anu that close the window.
B) Mother requested Anu to close the window.
C) Mother said Anu closed the window.
D) Mother asked Anu that she closes the window.

Q7. He said, "Is this your book?"
A) He asked whether that was my book.
B) He asked whether was that my book.
C) He said that this is your book.
D) He asked that is this my book.

Q8. The doctor said to the patient, "Take the medicine regularly."
A) The doctor advised the patient to take the medicine regularly.
B) The doctor said that the patient takes the medicine regularly.
C) The doctor asked the patient that take medicine.
D) The doctor advised that the patient took the medicine.

Q9. The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the Sun."
A) The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the Sun.
B) The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the Sun.
C) The teacher said that the Earth had revolved around the Sun.
D) The teacher asked whether the Earth revolves around the Sun.

Q10. She said to me, "Will you help me tomorrow?"
A) She asked me if I would help her the next day.
B) She asked me if I will help me tomorrow.
C) She told me whether I would help her tomorrow.
D) She asked that would I help her the next day.

ANSWER KEY: 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-A, 5-A, 6-B, 7-A, 8-A, 9-B, 10-A.

VOCABULARY
Prudent = careful and sensible.
Reluctant = unwilling or hesitant.
Lucid = clear and easy to understand.
Obsolete = no longer in use.
Resilient = able to recover from difficulty.
Write one original sentence for each.

ACTIVE MICRO-TOPIC: VENN-DIAGRAM COUNTING.
STATUS: NEW FOCUSED APPLICATION.

For two sets:
n(A∪B) = n(A)+n(B)-n(A∩B).

For three sets:
n(A∪B∪C) = n(A)+n(B)+n(C)-n(A∩B)-n(B∩C)-n(C∩A)+n(A∩B∩C).

The triple overlap is added once because it was subtracted three times.

Q1. 40 students like tea, 30 like coffee and 20 like both. How many like at least one?
A) 40 B) 50 C) 60 D) 70

Q2. 28 students like Maths, 24 like Science and 10 like both. How many like exactly one?
A) 32 B) 42 C) 52 D) 62

Q3. 50 study Hindi, 35 study English and 15 study both. If there are 80 students, how many study neither?
A) 5 B) 10 C) 15 D) 20

Q4. 30 use A, 25 use B, 20 use C; 10 use A&B, 8 use B&C, 7 use C&A, and 5 use all three. How many use at least one?
A) 55 B) 60 C) 65 D) 70

Q5. 45 play cricket, 32 play football and 18 play both. How many play only cricket?
A) 13 B) 18 C) 27 D) 32

Q6. n(A)=52, n(B)=41 and n(A∪B)=70. Find n(A∩B).
A) 13 B) 21 C) 23 D) 29

Q7. A∩B=12, B∩C=9, C∩A=8 and A∩B∩C=5. Find the sum of the three pairwise-only regions.
A) 9 B) 14 C) 19 D) 24

Q8. 55 read newspaper X, 45 read Y and 20 read both. Out of 100, how many read neither?
A) 10 B) 15 C) 20 D) 25

Q9. 38 know Excel, 30 know Word and 16 know both. How many know exactly one?
A) 36 B) 38 C) 52 D) 54

Q10. n(A)=25, n(B)=22, n(C)=18, pairwise intersections are 8, 6 and 5, and triple intersection is 3. Find the union.
A) 46 B) 47 C) 49 D) 52

ANSWER KEY: 1-B, 2-A, 3-B, 4-A, 5-C, 6-C, 7-B, 8-C, 9-A, 10-C.
CHECKS: Q4=55; Q7=(12-5)+(9-5)+(8-5)=14; Q10=49.

ACTIVE MICRO-TOPIC: COMPOUND INTEREST WITH HALF-YEARLY COMPOUNDING.
STATUS: NEW FOCUSED APPLICATION.

Half-yearly rate = annual rate ÷ 2.
Number of periods = years × 2.
Amount = P(1+r/200)^(2t).

Q1. Amount on ₹10,000 at 10% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 1 year?
A) ₹11,000 B) ₹11,025 C) ₹11,100 D) ₹11,210

Q2. CI on ₹8,000 at 20% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 1 year?
A) ₹1,600 B) ₹1,680 C) ₹1,728 D) ₹1,760

Q3. Amount on ₹5,000 at 8% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 1 year?
A) ₹5,400 B) ₹5,408 C) ₹5,416 D) ₹5,432

Q4. Effective annual rate for 12% p.a. compounded half-yearly?
A) 12% B) 12.36% C) 12.72% D) 13.20%

Q5. Amount on ₹20,000 at 10% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 2 years?
A) ₹24,000 B) ₹24,310.125 C) ₹24,500 D) ₹25,000

Q6. CI on ₹16,000 at 25% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 1 year?
A) ₹4,000 B) ₹4,250 C) ₹4,500 D) ₹4,750

Q7. CI on ₹12,000 at 10% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 2 years?
A) ₹2,586.075 B) ₹2,650 C) ₹2,762 D) ₹2,900

Q8. CI on ₹25,000 at 20% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 1 year?
A) ₹5,000 B) ₹5,250 C) ₹5,500 D) ₹5,750

Q9. Amount on ₹10,000 at 6% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 2 years?
A) ₹11,236.48 B) ₹11,255.0881 C) ₹11,300 D) ₹11,360

Q10. Amount on ₹10,000 at 20% p.a., compounded half-yearly for 2 years?
A) ₹14,641 B) ₹14,400 C) ₹14,880 D) ₹15,000

CHECKED KEY
1-B: 10000×1.05²=11025.
2-B: 8000×1.10²=9680, so CI=1680.
3-B: 5000×1.04²=5408.
4-B: 1.06²-1=12.36%.
5-B: 20000×1.05⁴=24310.125.
6-B: 16000×1.125²=20250, so CI=4250.
7-A: 12000×1.05⁴=14586.075, so CI=2586.075.
8-B: 25000×1.10²=30250, so CI=5250.
9-B: 10000×1.03⁴=11255.0881.
10-A: 10000×1.10⁴=14641.

FOCUS: FILES, FOLDERS AND EXTENSIONS.

Definition: A file stores information. A folder organizes files and subfolders.

DISTINCTIONS
• .docx = Word document.
• .xlsx = spreadsheet.
• .pptx = presentation.
• .pdf = portable document format.
• .jpg/.png = image formats.
• Copy creates a duplicate.
• Move changes the location of an existing item.
• Rename changes the name; it does not convert the format.

COMMON MISTAKES
• Renaming photo.jpg to photo.pdf does not convert it.
• Do not open unknown executable attachments casually.
• Use meaningful folder names.

HANDS-ON TASK, 15 MINUTES
1. Create SSC_CHSL_2026.
2. Inside create English, Reasoning, Quant, GA, Computer, Typing, Current_Affairs.
3. Create Day3_Notes.txt.

6. Create Revision_Queue.txt in the main folder.
7. Move Revision_Queue.txt into English.
8. Check every extension.
9. Write today's mistakes in Revision_Queue.txt.
10. Keep the original Day3_Notes.txt.

SELF-TEST

2. Copy creates a duplicate while Move changes location. True/False?
3. Renaming .jpg to .pdf converts it? A)Yes B)No
4. Main purpose of a folder? A)Increase RAM B)Organize files C)Encrypt everything D)Convert files
5. Presentation extension? A).pptx B).xlsx C).txt D).csv

Fresh 10-minute passage:

Public administration depends on accurate records, clear communication and timely decisions. A well-organised office does not merely store information; it makes information easier to find, verify and use. Digital systems can improve speed, but accuracy remains essential because a small typing error may change a name, number, date or reference. A responsible employee therefore checks important entries before submitting a document. Files should be given meaningful names and placed in suitable folders so that another person can understand the structure without repeated explanations. In a busy office, good habits save time. Reading a sentence before typing it, keeping both hands correctly positioned, and correcting repeated mistakes can gradually improve speed and accuracy. The goal of typing practice is not to chase speed for one session. It is to build reliable performance that remains stable when the passage becomes unfamiliar. During practice, maintain a steady rhythm, avoid unnecessary backspacing, and focus on complete words rather than individual letters. After the test, record the result honestly. The error pattern is often more useful than raw speed because it tells you what needs correction. If numbers, punctuation or capital letters cause repeated mistakes, practise those elements separately before another timed passage. Consistency is built through short, focused sessions repeated over time.

Words typed: ______
Errors: ______
WPM: ______
Accuracy: ______
Error pattern: ______
Time: 10 minutes

WPM = words typed ÷ 10 if your platform reports raw words.
Record the first attempt honestly, then do a 5-minute correction drill.
